li.title: The Mists Do Not Follow You Here
li.text: The mists came again tonight, the way they come everywhere, and nobody barred the door against them. In the city that would have been unthinkable. Out here there is no obligator to report it to and no one left to be frightened on your behalf. One of the older ones stood in the doorway a long while and did not come back in until morning.

li.title: What Grows Under Ash
li.text: Skaa are not taught to farm for themselves. They are taught to farm for a lord and to hand it all over. Someone here remembered the difference. The ash still falls and the ground still refuses most things, but there is a plot cleared behind the huts now, and it belongs to nobody but you.

li.title: A Canton Clerk Asks After You
li.text: A tin-eared beggar on the trade road brings word for the price of a meal. Somewhere in the Canton of Inquisition a clerk has opened a file, written a number in it, and gone back to his tea. That is all it is so far. That is how it always starts.

li.title: The Obligator's Confession
li.text: The beggar comes back, and this time he wants more than a meal. An obligator was caught skimming from the Ministry's own coffers and traded his life for a confession before the end. He spoke of a vault sealed since the Ascension, holding a single bead of lerasium - the metal the Lord Ruler himself was made from. The Ministry does not admit the vault exists. The obligator is already dead. The vault is not.

li.title: The Seam Was a Splinter
li.text: The survivor talks more freely now that there is atium on the table and none of it went to an obligator. The seam he sent you to was nothing, he says. A crack. The Pits themselves are half a day further in and they are not a mine at all - they are worked, by skaa, under guard, and have been since before anyone's grandfather. That is where the Lord Ruler's atium comes from. All of it.
